query: The Crystal on the Sill {On the windowsill sits somebody's abandoned crystal experiment, a jar of blue spikes labelled DO NOT FEED.|The crystal has grown out of its jar and halfway down the wall. The label now reads DO NOT FEED (WE MEAN IT).|The crystal reaches the floor now and has started on the next window. Someone has given it a name and a little hat.} {It chimes faintly when the door slams.|It has grown a new spike toward the warmest cauldron.|{season == "winter": Frost and crystal are racing each other up the glass.|In the afternoon light it throws blue all over the benches.}} Feed it a pinch of salt {It drinks the salt with a sound like a sigh and grows one perfect new spike. You understand, suddenly, how it's built.|A new spike unfolds slowly, like a fern. You sketch the growth, and it makes sense of a whole chapter.|It grows a spike in your exact direction, which is either affection or aim. You take notes either way.} {It shoots out a spike the size of a finger and catches your sleeve and your wrist. The label, you concede, was right.|It grows a spike straight through your notes and into your thumb. You are not the first; there's a list.|It sneezes crystal dust all over you. You sparkle blue until bedtime and itch till morning.} Snap off a spike for Pell's {Pell & Daughters pays well for clean crystal, no questions asked. The jar seems to notice the gap.|You snap off a spike while it's busy growing toward the cauldron. It chimes once, sharply, as if taking your name. Pell's pays anyway.|You break off a piece from the bottom where nobody will notice and sell it in the village. The little hat tilts at you when you come back.}
